module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 713

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/713](https://www.erdosproblems.com/713)
- [Er67d] Erdős, P., *Some recent results on extremal problems in graph theory. {R}esults*. (1967),
  117--123 (English); pp. 124--130 (French).
- [ErSi70] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Some extremal problems in graph theory*. Combinatorial
  theory and its applications, I-III (Proc. Colloq., Balatonfüred, 1969) (1970), 377-390.
- [FrFu87] Frankl, P. and Füredi, Z., *Exact solution of some Turán-type problems*. J. Combin.
  Theory Ser. A (1987), 226--262.
- [FuGe21] Füredi, Zoltán and Gerbner, Dániel, *Hypergraphs without exponents*. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (2021), Paper No. 105517, 9.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos713

open scoped Classical in
/--
Is it true that, for every bipartite graph $G$, there exists some $\alpha\in [1,2)$ and $c>0$ such that $$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\sim cn^\alpha?$$

The condition that $G$ have at least two edges excludes degenerate forbidden graphs whose
extremal number is eventually zero, for which the displayed asymptotic with $c>0$ is impossible.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_713.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), G.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∃ α c : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 ∧ 0 < c ∧
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => c * (n : ℝ) ^ α) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Must $\alpha$ be rational?

The same nondegeneracy condition on $G$ is used as in part (i). Rationality means that the real
number $\alpha$ lies in the image of the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{R}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_713.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), G.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∀ α c : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 → 0 < c →
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => c * (n : ℝ) ^ α) →
        α ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos713

reformulations.difference: Erdős (1981), §III.2, and the archived problem page use an offset exponent a ∈ [0,1) and a finite positive limit after division by n^(1+a). Lean uses the total exponent α ∈ [1,2) and asymptotic equivalence to c*n^α. The 1967 and 1981 papers also use the forcing threshold, rather than the maximum number of edges in a forbidden-subgraph-free graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Set α = 1+a, with inverse a = α−1. For c>0, Mathlib's IsEquivalent here is equivalent to ex(n,G)/n^α tending to c: c*n^α is eventually positive. The papers' forcing threshold is ex(n,G)+1, and adding 1 leaves this asymptotic unchanged because α≥1. The reparameterization/limit equivalence and invariance under adding 1 were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The 1981 source asks whether its offset exponent a in the positive-limit formula is always rational. Lean instead asks whether the total exponent α in ex(n,G) ∼ c*n^α belongs to the image of ℚ in ℝ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two exponents satisfy α=1+a, so α is rational exactly when a is rational. The bounds and asymptotic hypotheses correspond as in part (i). The universal implication correctly asks about exponents for which the positive asymptotic exists; it does not assume a positive answer to the separate existence question. The conditional statements' equivalence under this reparameterization was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Both declarations were checked; no mathematical defect was found. The two-edge restriction appropriately makes the nondegenerate domain explicit. Lean checks verified that the three-vertex path satisfies the hypotheses, graphs on at most two vertices cannot satisfy them, extremalNumber is zero at n=0 and n=1, ex(2,P3)=1, and the single-edge forbidden graph has extremal number zero. Admissible forbidden graphs always have a forbidden-subgraph-free host, so the empty-supremum convention causes no issue. All final scratch checks compiled without errors or warnings, without using the problem's sorry-backed theorems as proofs. Live access to erdosproblems.com/713 was blocked by Cloudflare; the archived page, all four cited papers, and the archive's original 1981 reference were read instead. The 1981 reference explicitly verifies the rationality follow-up. The current separate problem database records #713 as open; the cited hypergraph counterexamples and the disproved narrower list of possible exponents do not settle either declaration.
